item.description: South Korea will toughen penalties for illegal drone flights and move to restore a no-fly zone near the border to prevent inter-Korean incidents, Unification Minister Chung Dong-young announced Wednesday, formally expressing regret to North Korea over alleged drone incursions. item.title: Kim Jong Un formally deploys 50 new tactical nuke launchers at ceremony
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un officially deployed 50 new launch vehicles for the country’s 600mm rocket system at a ceremony on Wednesday, according to state media, a type of missile primarily targeting South Korea that allegedly “incorporates artificial intelligence (AI)” and can be equipped with nuclear warheads. item.title: Asian youth table tennis tournament relocated from North Korea to Oman
item.description: A youth table tennis tournament scheduled to be held in North Korea later this year has been relocated to Oman, following reports that the organizer was unable to secure entry visas for mandatory inspections. The 30th Asian Youth Table Tennis Championships will take place from June 22-28 Muscat, Oman, rather than in Pyongyang as originally […]

item.title: North Korean leader’s sister praises Seoul’s apology for drones, renews threats
item.description: The North Korean leader’s influential sister Kim Yo Jong expressed appreciation on Thursday for South Korea’s acknowledgement of repeated civilian drone incursions across the border, but warned of “terrible consequences” if there are further incidents. item.title: Kim Jong Un vows to ‘open new service sectors’ at launch of construction project
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended a groundbreaking ceremony for the fifth stage of construction in the Hwasong area of Pyongyang on Wednesday, according to state media, where he promised to open more “service sectors” to meet growing public demand. item.title: Yoon Suk Yeol sentenced to life in prison over martial law decree
item.description: A Seoul court found former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol guilty of being the “ringleader of an insurrection” and sentenced him to life imprisonment on Thursday, more than a year after his failed attempt to impose martial law to counter alleged “pro-North Korea” forces.
